verdict: Caution on Patna residential developers: lend only to NBCC-linked or RERA-clean local builders with escrow-controlled collections; avoid small unregistered developers and land-bank plays.
title: Patna residential real estate: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Patna developer buys land, gets RERA and municipal approvals, builds towers, and sells units on a construction-linked payment plan. **Cash comes in as booking advances and instalments, not as rent, so the lender is really financing construction against a receivables book.** The cycle is long: land cost is paid upfront, construction is paid monthly to contractors, and collections trail by the slab schedule. **So when a proposal lands, check the RERA registration number and the sanctioned plan first; if either is missing, ask why and stop.**

## Where value and cash sit
Value sits in the land bank and in sold-but-uncollected receivables; cash sits in the escrow account. **The single number that decides the loan is committed receivables divided by (pending construction cost plus debt outstanding) — collect from customer, because no Patna-specific figure exists in our sources.** Peer evidence shows what good looks like: Brigade's consolidated net debt was INR 2,765 crore against cash of INR 2,674 crore, with debt-to-equity at 0.31 [5], and ICRA noted a cash flow adequacy ratio of 98% for one large developer [8]. **If a Patna builder cannot show a similar cover, ask for the month-wise collection plan and the contractor schedule before sanctioning.**

## What has changed now
Two local facts matter. The Bihar cabinet has cleared NBCC redevelopment of Bahadurpur Housing Colony and an 8.5-acre Sector 5 project in Patna, both self-financed through the State Housing Board [1]. **If a borrower's sales pitch rests on mixed-use or home-office demand, ask for the approval status of each unit; unapproved commercial use is a demand risk, not an asset.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
Pursue mid-size local builders with a delivered project, clean RERA record, and buyers who are salaried or Bihar-government employees. **Structure every line with a tripartite escrow, construction-linked disbursement, and a covenant that collections route through the escrow; take the monthly escrow statement, the RERA progress report, and the sales register every month.** Avoid first-time developers, pure land aggregators, and anyone selling before approval. **If a borrower resists escrow or asks for a land-only facility, decline.**

## Early-warning signs
Watch booking cancellations, a widening gap between sold and collected, contractor payment delays, and any municipal notice on the project. **If cancellations rise or escrow inflows fall below the construction draw for two months, freeze disbursement and re-appraise.** Note that our peer and rating sources are national and dated — the ICRA reports are from 2024 and 2025 [8][9] — and Patna-specific data is thin, so lean on first principles and these local facts [1][2][3].
watch: Collections below construction draw for two consecutive months -> freeze disbursement and re-appraise
Construction behind schedule by more than one quarter -> seek revised cash flow and additional promoter support
Cancellations above 10% of bookings -> ask for buyer profile and re-price risk
Any notice on commercial use of residential units -> stop new sanctions on that project
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Municipal crackdown on 50,000-plus properties and new NBCC supply raise execution and demand risk for small Patna builders.
